questions.prompt: A compass needle is placed under a wire. When current flows, the needle…
questions.explain: A current produces a magnetic field around the wire.

questions.prompt: How can you make an electromagnet stronger? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: More turns, more current and an iron core all strengthen it.

questions.prompt: Why are electromagnets used in scrapyard cranes instead of permanent magnets?
options: They can be switched off to drop the scrap
questions.explain: Switch off the current and the magnetism disappears.

questions.prompt: In the lab, the current was reversed. What happened to the compass deflection?
questions.explain: Reversing the current reverses the magnetic field.

questions.prompt: An electromagnet with 50 turns and 2 cells holds 10 clips. Assuming clips held is proportional to turns × cells, how many clips would 100 turns and 2 cells hold?
questions.explain: Doubling the turns doubles the strength: 20 clips.

questions.prompt: Order how an electric bell rings.
steps: Pressing the switch completes the circuit
The electromagnet pulls the iron strip and the hammer hits the gong
Moving the strip breaks the circuit, so the magnet switches off
The strip springs back, completing the circuit again and repeating
questions.explain: Making and breaking the circuit repeatedly makes the hammer vibrate.

questions.prompt: Plan an investigation into how the number of turns affects the strength of an electromagnet.
questions.modelAnswer: Independent variable: number of turns (20, 40, 60, 80) wound on an iron nail. Dependent variable: the number of paper clips lifted. Control variables: the same nail, the same wire, the same number of cells (current), the same size of paper clips, and switching on for only a few seconds so the wire doesn't overheat. Repeat three times for each number of turns and plot a graph.
rubric: At least two controls, including current
questions.explain: Criterion B: plan a fair test.
